jess: Quick question about API contract for generation params — specifically stop sequences vs max_tokens behavior. If a stop sequence appears beyond the max_tokens cutoff, should client expect a truncated response with no stop matched? Are we normalizing/returning partial matches in logprobs?

mike: Short answer: we enforce max_tokens hard. If output reaches max_tokens we cut and return. Stop sequences are only checked while generating, so if the stop would occur after the cutoff it won't be seen. logprobs for truncated tokens will be present up to cutoff; there's no partial-stop marker.

kai: Hmm, do we return any flag that truncation happened? Clients want to know whether stop triggered vs max_tokens. Right now we only return final_token_count and the text. We should add a field or status code?

mike: Right now there's no explicit "truncated_by_max_tokens" boolean. We have an internal trace but not in the public contract. Adding a field is low-risk — worth a docs PR + SDK bump.

sam: Also a related Q: interplay temp/top_p. If user sets temperature=0 and top_p<1, do we do greedy (ignore top_p) or deterministic top-p filtering?

mike: Our runtime treats temp==0 as greedy; top_p is ignored in that branch. That's been the implementation since the sampler refactor, but docs don't call it out. So behavior: temp==0 -> argmax; otherwise sample using (temp, top_p) together.

jess: Ok, can we (1) open a docs PR clarifying temp==0 semantics, (2) add a boolean in response like "truncated": "max_tokens"|"stop"|"none"? Prefer enum string so existing clients parse.

kai: Agree on enum string. For backward compat we should make it optional and default omitted. SDKs can map missing -> null. Also add a small contract test that asserts presence in new version.

eval-bot: FYI regression: tests/api/gen/logprobs_truncation failing on main. Link: https://ci.redwood.ai/1234 — failing case expects logprobs for a stop token that never emitted. root cause = test assumed stop would be honored past max_tokens.

sam: I'll file the RFC+CR (#457) and ping infra for canary. @mike can you add a tiny change in the runtime to expose the decision reason in trace so it can be surfaced?

mike: Yep, I'll add trace hook and a response field. Will open PR tomorrow. @jess please add to the release checklist.

jess: Thanks — adding to checklist now. cc @kai for SDK bump strategy. :eyes: 

kai: I'll draft SDK bump and compatibility note. Quick check: any objections to string enum values ["none","stop","max_tokens"]? If no objections I'll proceed.

sam: fine by me. :+1:

jess: No objections. I'll update the docs PR title to include enum example and a short example request/response.

mike: And I'll add unit tests to ensure temp==0 path skips top_p. small checklist:
- docs PR
- runtime trace + response enum
- SDK bump
- canary test
- CI regression fix

jess: Great. Tagging this thread for async follow-up. Anyone want to pick the docs PR?

kai: I'll start the docs PR after I finish the SDK changes. ETA EOD tomorrow.

jess: Perfect, thanks all. :rocket:
